# Third-Party Reputation Findings, 24 Clark County New Construction Builders

**Prepared:** 2026-07-25
**Prepared by:** Third-Party Reputation Researcher
**Scope:** Clark County, Nevada. Pahrump, Mesquite, and Boulder City are excluded. See "Excluded rows log" at the bottom.

---

## READ THIS BEFORE USING ANY LINE BELOW

**Everything in this file is a record of what a named third party published, on the date shown, at the URL shown. Nothing here is an opinion of Ryan Rose or Rose Homes LV.**

Three hard rules for whoever turns this into guide prose:

1. **Do not add adjectives.** "The Better Business Bureau lists an A+ rating" is fine. "This builder is reputable" is not. "Reliable", "trusted", "top-rated", "troubled", and "problem builder" are all out.
2. **Do not rank, score, average, or order these builders.** Do not build a "best builders" list. Do not sort a table by rating or by complaint count. Do not add stars. The one exception is a study score that a third party itself published, and even then print it as that study's finding for that one builder, never as part of an ordering you created.
3. **Every line must carry the source URL and the retrieval date when it reaches a reader.** These records change weekly. A number printed without its date becomes a false statement within months.

**On complaint counts.** A BBB complaint count is a count of complaints filed, not a count of findings against the builder. Large builders close more homes and so tend to show larger raw counts. The guide must say this plainly next to any complaint number, or leave the numbers out entirely. Do not print a raw complaint count beside a small local builder's count and let a reader draw a conclusion from the gap.

**On license entities.** Big builders license through Nevada entities whose names do not match the brand on the sales trailer. Lennar builds under "Greystone Nevada LLC". Pulte builds under "P N II Inc". Signature Homes builds under "Plaster Development Company Inc". Those entity names are recorded below so a reader can find the right record. Do not present an entity name as a brand name.

**Note on the Nevada State Contractors Board search.** The NSCB public license search is a form POST and produces no permanent link to an individual license record. Every NSCB citation below therefore points at the public search page and states the exact search that reproduces the record. The NSCB license detail page carries a section headed "Disciplinary Action During Last 5 Years" when such an action exists. Where a line below says no such section appears, that means the section was absent from the public record on 2026-07-25. It does not mean no action exists outside that five year window, and it does not mean no action is pending.

## The studies, described once

Print this block, or a shortened version of it, wherever the guide first mentions any study result. A score with no method attached is not usable information.

**Lifestory Research 2026 America's Most Trusted Home Builder Study.** Lifestory Research collected 62,596 opinions from people across the United States who indicated they were actively shopping for a new home over the previous 12 months, in the largest United States housing markets, and rated the 20 largest home builders in the country. Respondents had to be actively considering a purchase and familiar with a brand before rating its trustworthiness. The output is a Net Trust Quotient Score per builder brand. The study is national. It does not publish a Las Vegas result [source: https://www.lifestoryresearch.com/2026-americas-most-trusted-home-builder-brands | verified: 2026-07-25]

**31st Annual Homebuyers' Choice Awards, published by Zonda, 2026.** Based on more than 210,000 verified homebuyer surveys collected through TrustBuilder CX powered by Eliant, covering more than 250 homebuilders nationwide. The surveys cover the purchase, the move-in, and the first year of ownership. Awards are given by category and by builder division, so a division level result can be city specific [source: https://zondahome.com/31st-annual-homebuyers-choice-awards/ | verified: 2026-07-25]

**23rd Annual AvidCX Awards, published by ECI Software Solutions, announced 2026-05-26.** 511 qualifying builders participated. The program analyzed homebuyer data on satisfaction, referrals, and key experience metrics from January through December 2025. No Las Vegas or Nevada division winner appears in the published winner list reviewed [source: https://www.ecisolutions.com/blog/2026-avidcx-homebuilder-awards/ | verified: 2026-07-25] and [source: https://www.ecisolutions.com/news/eci-2026-avidcx-awards-top-homebuilders-north-america/ | verified: 2026-07-25]

**J.D. Power New-Home Builder Customer Satisfaction Study: there is no current one.** J.D. Power cancelled its 2011 U.S. New-Home Builder Customer Satisfaction Study, citing difficult market conditions in residential construction and a smaller pool of builders to evaluate, and said it would continue to monitor conditions to assess the timing of re-introducing the study. No later edition of that study was found. The most recent edition located is 2010, in which Las Vegas appeared among the markets with the highest overall satisfaction [source: https://www.custombuilderonline.com/home/article/55174563/jd-power-scraps-2011-us-new-home-builder-customer-satisfaction-study | verified: 2026-07-25] and [source: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/jd-power-and-associates-reports--satisfaction-with-new-home-builders-and-new-home-quality-reach-historic-highs-as-home-builders-respond-to-tough-market-conditions-by-improving-products-and-service-102944659.html | verified: 2026-07-25]

**Consequence for the guide:** any Las Vegas builder marketing that cites "J.D. Power" for new-home builder satisfaction is citing something from 2010 or earlier. If a builder's sales office shows a J.D. Power claim, ask what year and what study. Do not repeat such a claim in the guide.

## Method, so this can be reproduced or challenged

- **Better Business Bureau.** Each builder was located through the BBB directory search at https://www.bbb.org/search with the location set to Las Vegas, NV. Where no Las Vegas area profile existed, the company headquarters profile was used and is labeled as such in the builder's section. For each profile, the main profile page was read for the letter rating and accreditation status, and the profile's `/complaints` sub-page was read for complaint counts. Both URLs are cited.
- **Nevada State Contractors Board.** Each builder was searched at https://app.nvcontractorsboard.com/Clients/NVSCB/Public/ContractorLicenseSearch/ContractorLicenseSearch.aspx using the Company Name mode with wildcards, then each returned license was opened to its detail record and read for status, status date, origin date, expiration date, classification, monetary limit, and the presence of a "Disciplinary Action During Last 5 Years" section. The search is a form POST and produces no permanent per-license URL, so each citation names the search that reproduces the record.
- **Studies.** Only named studies that publish a method were used. Anonymous review-site star averages, Zillow builder profiles, Yelp, Houzz, and Google review counts were deliberately excluded and must not be added later.
- **What was not checked.** Clark County and City of Las Vegas building permit histories, Nevada Secretary of State entity standing, Nevada District Court construction defect filings, and any NRS Chapter 40 notices. Those are real public records and any of them could change the picture. They were outside this task's scope and are marked here so nobody assumes they were covered.
